full_judgment:
3. According to the plaintiff, the suit land originally belonged to Golak Chandra Shil in whose name R.S. Khatian was correctly prepared. He died leaving behind his only son, Baburam who died leaving behind two wives, namely Janaki Bala and Hemanta Bala and a daughter Shaila Bala through his wife Janaki Bala. After the death of Baburam the 1st schedule land devolved upon his two wives who were in possession in equal shares and by amicable partition Janaki Bala got 3 gondas of land from the southern side and Hemanta Bala got 3 gondas share on the northern side. Baburam had a brother Sadhuram, who died after him leaving behind one son namely Chintaharan who died leaving behind his only son, Santosh Kumar Shil Chintaharan used to manage the property on behalf of Hemanta Bala Hemanta Bala transferred her 3 gondas of land by registered deed dated 09.07.1946 to Santosh Kumar Shil, but in order to save the registration fees the sale deed was registered as a deed of gift. After death of Janaki Bala her 3 gondas of land were transferred by her daughter Sahila Bala and possession of the same was delivered to the purchasers. Aforementioned Santosh Kumar Shil being co-sharer in the suit jote on the basis of the deed of gift dated 09.07.1946 filed a preemption case  being No. 41 of 1973 in the Court of 3rd Subordinate Judge, Chittagong and the pre-emption case was allowed in favour of the preemptor Santosh Kumar Shil. An appeal by the pre-emptee before the District Judge, Chittagong was dismissed on compromise and as per term of the compromise the order of preemption became absolute and Santos; Kumar Shil became the 16 annas owner of the 6 gondas of land left by Janaki Bala and Hemanta Bala. During the PS. operation the suit land was recorded in the name of Shaila Bala and her husband but the B.S. Khatian was recorded in the name of Santosh Kumar Shil who transferred 3 gondas of land from the southern side to Gopal Krishna and his wife Chinu Bala who were inducted into physical possession thereof. Santosh Kumar Shill transferred 1½ gondas of land to the plaintiff by registered deed of gift dated 24.11.1982 and the remaining 1½ gondas of land were transferred to the plaintiffs other brother defendant No. 2 by a deed of gift dated 15.07.1986 and physical possession was transferred thereof to the plaintiff and defendant No. 2 thereby the entire interest in the suit land of Santosh Kumar Shil was exhausted. The plaintiff and the defendant No. 2 constructed two houses in their suit land consisting of six rooms and by amicable settlement the plaintiff has been in possession of two of the rooms on the southern side and in one room one Milon Chandra Dey was a tenant under the plaintiff who vacated the room in the 1st part of November, 1991 and handed over physical possession to the plaintiff. The plaintiff’s father died on 10.11.1991 and while he was busy there the defendant No. 1 dispossessed the plaintiff from the said room on 20.11.1991. The defendant No.1 is the son of Shaila Bala (grandson of Janaki Bala) who had no possession in any part of the "Ka" schedule land or "Kha" schedule land before 20.11.1991. Hemanta Bala had transferred her share f the land to Santosh Kumar Shil in the year 1946 and left the suit premises and resided at the house of her sister where she died subsequently. On the death of Hemanta Bala defendant No. 1 never claimed any right, title and possession on the suit land and also did not challenge the legality of the deed of gift dated 09.07.1946. The claim of the plaintiff is that the defendant No. 1 has no right, title and valid possession of the suit land. 

 8. In its judgment, the High Court in Division observed that the plaintiff had filed rent receipts to show that he paid a the land revenue and Municipal taxes and also proved that the other rooms situated on the suit plots are being possessed by him. The defendant No. 1 neither claimed that the other rooms situated on the suit plots are not possessed by hire nor he stated as to how those rooms went being possessed by the plaintiff rhea High Court Division further observance that the defendant No.1 proved that the P.S. record was prepared in the name of Shaila Bala and her husband but the subsequent B.S. Khatian in respect of the suit plot was prepared in the name oil Santosh Kumar Shil (vendor of they plaintiff). The High Court Division also observed from the evidence and materials on record that the plaintiff succeeded in proving his uninterrupted possessor in the suit land since 1946 till his dispose session by the defendant. The High Court Division finally observed from the evidence on record that Hemanta Bala died in 1968 but till date the defender had not taken any step against the of gift dated 9.7.1946. Although subsequently Santosh Kumar Shill transferred some portion of the suit plot by seven registered deeds, from the evidence appeared that the defendants No. 1 enter into one room in the suit plot by dispossessing the plaintiff on 20.11.1991. As per Article 141 of the Limitation Act the reversionary had to file a suit within years from the date of death of Hemanta Bala in 1968 but he failed to take any step and, therefore, the plaintiffs predecessor had acquired valid right and title in the suit land on the basis of the deed of gift and the plaintiff had acquired an adverse title in the suit land.
